note: 25 skills enumerated under framework/skills/ at pinned commit 317ede0f594cda80f0d84b11098afac0c29e21b1 (MIT, repo-root LICENSE). The task capped vendoring at 6; silver-research, silver-synthesize, silver-evaluate, silver-measure, silver-ideate, and silver-structure were vendored (see their own manifests). The 19 skills below were rejected. All 25 share an identical file shape (SKILL.md + skill.yaml + agents/openai.yaml + scripts/invoke.mjs, invoke.mjs byte-identical across every one) and an identical ~30-40-line four-step-workflow/Done/Boundaries template whose 'Done' step instructs writing output through a `.silver/bin/silver invoke` CLI that belongs to the parent Silver Design Framework npm package or an installer-generated `.silver/runtime/` directory -- neither of which is bundleable (the framework/ directory alone spans activities, guardrails, migrations, playbooks, protocols, providers, runtime, scenarios, schemas, scripts, semantic-roles, studio-voice, testing, transports, well over the 25-file bundling cap, and installer/*.mjs is ~30 additional files). Every skill below was read in full (SKILL.md at minimum; frontmatter for all) at the pinned SHA before scoring.

rejectedSkills.reason: Thin (35-line) brand-foundations checklist (promise, feeling, attributes, anti-attributes, positioning) with no concrete brand-development technique or example; overlaps existing apple-design/design-system-governance brand guidance; same repo-wide CLI host-coupling.

Legitimate evidence-gathering step (source provenance, observation-vs-interpretation separation) but the thinnest of the research-adjacent skills (4 generic lines) and redundant once silver-research and silver-synthesize are vendored from this same repo; cut to respect the task's 6-skill cap for this repository, preferring the four explicitly named priority categories plus research and structure.

Component-contract/anatomy/accessibility-documentation workflow overlaps design-tokens, design-system-governance, and pick-ui-library territory directly; generic and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

A meta-skill whose entire purpose is discovering and running OTHER checks defined elsewhere in the framework's own check registry (conformance, browser, a11y, responsive, interaction, provenance, asset, presentation, production) -- it defines no checks itself, so it is unusable without the full framework, worse than its siblings on conformance. Heavily overlaps a11y-check-page, design-review, and frontend-design-review, already in the registry.

Task/interaction/component-state-machine flow modeling overlaps the vendored silver-structure (this batch, which explicitly hands off sequences to flow) and silver-map; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Rebuilds accepted design intent into 'the local production recipe under production policy' -- both the recipe and the policy are framework-defined artifacts not present in the skill directory, so this is unusable without the full framework even more than its siblings. Overlaps design-engineering territory the registry already covers more concretely (frontend-design-review).

Journey map / service blueprint / experience map / ecosystem map skill that directly overlaps service-blueprint, already in the registry, for its primary use case; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Evidence-linked opportunity/proposal/outcome-change case for stakeholders directly overlaps design-negotiation, already in the registry (both build the case for a design decision with before/after, tradeoffs, and a decision request); thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Built around reading and proposing changes to a 'My Practice' personal-lesson store that is a Silver-specific concept never defined or bundled in the skill directory -- effectively meaningless outside the full framework, and low relevance to product-design deliverables (it's a personal retrospective mechanism, not a design activity).

Design-decision-principles-with-examples workflow overlaps design-system-governance's principle-setting territory; thin (no worked example of a principle, tradeoff rule, or decision test) and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Product audience/JTBD/outcomes/positioning foundations; not among the task's named priority categories (research synthesis, ideation, evaluation, measurement) and thinner than the 6 selected skills; cut to respect the 6-skill cap for this repository.

Exact-concept collision with the registry's already-vendored 'prototype' skill (interactive-prototype tag), and far thinner (no fidelity guidance, no tooling specifics) than what's already vendored; CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Entirely a sync/merge-conflict-resolution tool between a portable artifact and a linked repository or Figma -- every step is a `silver sync status|inspect|apply` CLI invocation with provider transports defined elsewhere in the framework; zero standalone value and not a design-content skill.

Living design-specification workflow (outcomes, scope, requirements, states, edge cases, accessibility, success criteria); not among the task's named priority categories and thinner than the 6 selected skills; cut to respect the 6-skill cap for this repository.

Semantic tokens, color ramps, typography roles, component/pattern registries, deprecations, migrations -- overlaps design-tokens, design-system-governance, and token-build directly; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.
Semantic themes, modes, and mappings directly overlaps theme-factory, already in the registry; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

Static visual representations of a proposed product experience at varying fidelity overlaps prototype, frontend-design, and canvas-design, already in the registry; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.
Product tone, voice, terminology, and context-specific content guidance directly overlaps ux-writing, already in the registry; thin and CLI-gated like the rest of the repo.

A workspace-status / next-action-recommender that inspects Silver-specific manifest, lock, checkpoint, and binding files (`.silver/bin/silver what-now .`) -- essentially project management over the framework's own state, not a design-content skill, and completely non-functional without the framework's generated workspace files.
